The test image shows a **leaf** with a large irregular tan/brown necrotic lesion along one margin, bordered by a distinct yellow-green halo. No visible fungal structures. This narrows candidates to 16 leaf classes.

Top candidates: **Bacterial_Blight** (yellow-green halos around brown lesions), **Sudden_death_syndrome** (interveinal necrosis), **Septoria_brown_spot** (dark brown lesions).

Let me view reference images one at a time.
Bacterial Blight ref shows small angular spots with yellow halos — the test image has a much larger marginal lesion. Less convincing match. Let me check Sudden Death Syndrome.
SDS shows classic interveinal necrosis with green veins — very different pattern from the test image's single large marginal lesion. Let me check Septoria brown spot.
Let me look at a second Bacterial Blight image — the first showed early-stage small spots, but the description says they can merge into large patches.
Still not matching well. Let me check Downy mildew and Brown Stem Rot — both can produce large coalescing lesions on leaves.
Downy mildew shows small scattered pale spots — not matching. Let me check Brown Stem Rot leaf symptoms.
BSR shows interveinal chlorosis — not matching. Let me check Frogeye leaf spot for comparison.
Let me use my last view on the third Bacterial Blight image to check if it shows advanced/merged lesion stage.

**Assessment summary:**

- Test image: single large irregular tan/brown necrotic lesion along the leaf margin with a clear yellow-green transition border
- Bacterial Blight refs: show early-stage small angular spots with yellow-green halos — the description explicitly states these "often merge to form large, dead patches on leaves; surrounded by yellowish-green halos"
- SDS: interveinal necrosis with green veins — ruled out
- Septoria brown spot: many small dark brown spots — ruled out
- Downy mildew: small scattered pale spots — ruled out
- Brown Stem Rot: interveinal chlorosis — ruled out
- Frogeye: small circular gray spots with reddish borders — ruled out

The large coalesced brown necrotic patch with a pronounced yellow-green halo is the hallmark of advanced Bacterial Blight where multiple angular lesions have merged. No other leaf disease in the candidate list produces this pattern of marginal necrosis with a yellowish-green border on an otherwise healthy green leaf.
